name: Colossus (xAI)
scale: 2 GW site capacity
description: The world's largest single-coherent AI training cluster as of early 2026, built in a former Electrolux factory in south Memphis. xAI added a third building ("Macrohardrr") in Dec. 2025, pushing site capacity toward 2 GW and a stated goal of 1 million GPUs.

controversy.summary: xAI ran dozens of unpermitted gas turbines at the site for over a year, in a majority-Black South Memphis neighborhood already burdened with industrial pollution (cancer risk ~4x the national average in nearby Boxtown). Studies link the turbines to a sharp rise in local nitrogen dioxide levels; the Southern Environmental Law Center and Earthjustice sued on behalf of the NAACP, and a U.S. Senator opened an investigation into the unpermitted operation.

links.title: SELC: "xAI built an illegal power plant"

name: Stargate Abilene (Site 1)
scale: 1.2 GW planned (8 buildings; ~0.6 GW online mid-2026)
description: Flagship Stargate campus, built by Crusoe on a 1,100-acre site. The most advanced of the seven announced U.S. Stargate locations; several buildings already energized and training workloads running.

name: Stargate Milam County
scale: Part of ~9 GW combined Stargate U.S. buildout
description: One of two additional Texas Stargate sites (alongside Shackelford County); hardware to be owned by SoftBank rather than Oracle.

name: Stargate Shackelford County
scale: Part of ~9 GW combined Stargate U.S. buildout
description: Third Texas Stargate site, near Abilene.

name: Stargate Doña Ana County
scale: Part of ~9 GW combined Stargate U.S. buildout
description: New Mexico Stargate site.

name: Stargate Lordstown
scale: Part of ~9 GW combined Stargate U.S. buildout
description: Ohio Stargate site, ground broken with an advanced data center design; hardware owned by SoftBank.

name: Stargate Port Washington ("Lighthouse")
scale: Part of ~9 GW combined Stargate U.S. buildout
description: Wisconsin Stargate site, just north of Milwaukee, built by Vantage Data Centers under the campus name "Lighthouse."

name: Stargate Saline Township ("The Barn")
scale: Part of ~9 GW combined Stargate U.S. buildout
description: Michigan Stargate site, southwest of Detroit, developed by Related Digital under the campus name "The Barn."

name: Hyperion
scale: 2 GW initial, public path to 5 GW; ~4M sq ft, 2,250 acres
description: Meta's largest announced data center, in rural northeast Louisiana. Entergy is building 10 gas-fired plants to power it; Meta has separately committed to 2.5 GW of new renewables, 240 miles of transmission lines and battery storage.

name: Prometheus
scale: ~1 GW
description: Billed as one of the highest-capacity data centers in the world when it opens in 2026, built using rapid-deployment tent-like structures plus an on-site gas power plant. Located in the New Albany, Ohio data-center corridor alongside Google, AWS and Microsoft facilities.

name: Fairwater (Wisconsin)
gpu_type: Hundreds of thousands of NVIDIA GB200/GB300
scale: Anchor site of Microsoft's distributed "AI superfactory"
description: First of Microsoft's Fairwater AI datacenters, networked directly to the Atlanta site via a dedicated long-haul AI WAN so the two function as one distributed supercomputer.

name: Fairwater (Atlanta)
gpu_type: NVIDIA GB200/GB300 (hundreds of thousands across the network)
scale: Second node of Microsoft's distributed "AI superfactory"
description: Second Fairwater site, brought online in October 2025, sharing Wisconsin's two-story, no-UPS/no-genset design and linked to it as a single logical training supercomputer.

name: Project Rainier
gpu_type: ~500,000 AWS Trainium2 chips (heading toward 1M+, plus Trainium3)
scale: 2.2 GW planned across 30 buildings (1,200-acre site)
description: Built for Anthropic to train and run Claude on AWS's own silicon rather than NVIDIA GPUs. Seven of an eventual 30 buildings were online as of late 2025, with nearly 1 GW of Trainium2/3 capacity targeted by end of 2026.

name: Council Bluffs TPU campus
gpu_type: Google TPU v7 "Ironwood" (Anthropic taking up to 1M chips)
scale: Part of >1 GW Anthropic-Google TPU expansion in 2026
description: One of Google's largest data center campuses, now racking the first of Anthropic's Ironwood TPU pods (9,216 chips each) as part of a deal for up to a million TPUs and over a gigawatt of capacity.

name: Stargate UAE
operator: G42 / OpenAI / Oracle / SoftBank / Cisco / NVIDIA
scale: First 200 MW phase live 2026; campus planned to reach 5 GW over ~19.2 km²
description: The largest announced AI data center campus outside the United States, anchored by G42 and operated jointly with OpenAI and Oracle. First 200 MW cluster targeted for 2026; full build envisions 5 GW powered by a mix of nuclear, solar and gas.

name: Mistral AI Campus (Bruyères-le-Châtelet)
scale: 44 MW initial; roadmap to 200 MW by 2027 and part of a planned 1.4-3 GW Paris-region campus by 2030
description: France's flagship sovereign-AI cluster, south of Paris, backed by a joint venture between Mistral AI, Nvidia, France's Bpifrance and Abu Dhabi's MGX aiming to build Europe's largest AI campus.

name: Stargate UK (Cobalt Park)
scale: ~8,000 GPUs offtake in early 2026, scaling toward 31,000
description: UK "AI Growth Zone" site built by Nscale. OpenAI initially committed to offtake compute here under Stargate UK, but paused its rental in 2026 citing high UK energy costs and regulatory uncertainty; Nscale's build continues with Microsoft and Nvidia as partners.

name: Stargate Norway (Kvandal)
scale: 230 MW initial, expandable to 520 MW
description: OpenAI's first announced European data center, in the Arctic Circle near Narvik to exploit abundant local hydropower. OpenAI itself stepped back from renting the capacity in April 2026; Microsoft is taking up the spare capacity instead, with the Nscale/Aker joint venture still building.

name: Stargate Argentina (Patagonia)
scale: 500 MW planned (first 100 MW phase ~2027)
description: OpenAI's first Latin American Stargate site, a letter-of-intent project with Argentine-US firm Sur Energy in southern Patagonia, framed as a $25bn investment. Exact location not yet finalized as of mid-2026, so the marker is placed at an approximate Patagonia location.

name: Reliance Intelligence AI Campus
scale: 120 MW commissioning end-2026, part of a $110B AI infrastructure commitment
description: India's largest announced AI compute campus, powered entirely by Reliance's Kutch solar platform. Meta is leasing 168 MW of capacity here for its first built-to-suit AI data center in India; framed by Reliance as part of a "sovereign AI backbone" for Indic-language models.

name: Stargate Korea (Southwest region)
scale: Not yet disclosed
description: SK Telecom signed an MoU with OpenAI to develop, build and operate an AI data center in southwest South Korea as part of Stargate's hardware-supply partnership with Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix (HBM memory). Exact site not yet disclosed; marker placed near the Saemangeum industrial zone, the region most associated with the announcement.

name: Alibaba Zhenwu Data Center
gpu_type: Domestic chips (Alibaba self-developed + Huawei Ascend ecosystem)
scale: Targeting ~100,000 chips
description: Part of China's push toward a domestic-chip AI computing grid (a reported $295B national plan to run 80% of capacity on Chinese silicon). Alibaba launched this Guangdong facility running on its own chips as Chinese firms commit over 500,000 combined Huawei Ascend chip orders for 2026.
